lessons.title: What HRA Is and Why It Shows Up in Your Salary Slip

body.text: HRA is the only big line on your payslip where the tax you pay depends on the rent you pay and the city you live in, not just on how much you earn. Two colleagues on identical salaries can pay very different tax on the same HRA.

children.text: Open your latest payslip on your company's HR portal, whether that is greytHR, Keka, Darwinbox or an email PDF. Below Basic Salary you will almost certainly see a line called House Rent Allowance. Most people know it has something to do with rent and tax. Very few can say how much of it is actually tax-free, or why. This lesson fixes that.
What HRA Actually Is

markDefs.definition: A fixed amount an employer pays on top of basic salary for a specific purpose, such as housing, travel or children's education. It is part of your salary and is taxable unless a specific exemption applies.
A salary component paid by an employer to help an employee meet the cost of renting a home. Part of it can be tax-free under the old tax regime if the employee actually pays rent.

children.text: An
allowance
is money your employer pays you on top of basic salary for a named purpose.
House Rent Allowance (HRA)
is the allowance meant for housing. It is paid to you every month as part of your salary, whether you rent a 1BHK in Koramangala, live with your parents in Lucknow or own a flat in Thane.
Here is a typical private-sector payslip. Rohan is a 28-year-old product analyst in Pune.

cells: Fixed by grade or CTC band
50% of basic, as per company policy
Balancing figure to reach the agreed pay
Before PF, professional tax and TDS

body.text: Rohan receives ₹25,000 of HRA every month no matter where he lives. What changes with his living arrangement is not the HRA he gets, but how much of it the tax law lets him treat as tax-free.

children.text: Why Employers Put HRA in Your Salary

HRA exists because housing is the single largest monthly cost for most salaried Indians, especially in large cities. Employers use it for three reasons: to reflect city living costs in pay, to follow a long-standing pay structure used by government and large employers, and because it lets employees who rent reduce their tax without the employer spending an extra rupee.

body.title: How HRA is fixed: government vs private sector

columns.label: Central government employees
points: Set by the 7th Pay Commission as a percentage of basic pay
30% in X-class cities, 20% in Y-class, 10% in Z-class
These rates apply since dearness allowance crossed 50% from January 2024
City class depends on population, not on the tax law's metro list

columns.label: Private-sector employees
points: Set by company policy, usually 40% or 50% of basic salary
Often 50% of basic for metro-based roles and 40% elsewhere
Some CTC structures let employees choose a higher or lower HRA
Can be restructured when basic salary changes

body.text: Do not confuse the 7th Pay Commission's X, Y and Z city classes with the tax law's 50% city list. The pay commission decides how much HRA a government employee receives. The Income-tax Rules decide how much of it is tax-free. They are set by different authorities and can change independently, so always check the tax list for the exemption. Lesson 6 covers it in detail.

children.text: Allowance vs Exemption: The Distinction That Matters

markDefs.definition: The portion of House Rent Allowance that is not counted as taxable income, available only to an employee who pays rent for the home they live in and has not chosen the new tax regime.

children.text: The HRA you receive is salary, and salary is taxable. What makes part of it tax-free is a separate rule: the
HRA exemption

. It now sits in Schedule III (Table: S. No. 11) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 10(13A) of the Income-tax Act, 1961), with the percentages and city list set by the Income-tax Rules, 2026. Whatever part of HRA is not exempt gets added to your taxable salary like any other allowance.

body.label: How much HRA is tax-free
body.context: Actual HRA received, rent paid minus 10% of salary, and 50% or 40% of salary depending on your city. Chapter 2 breaks down each limit.

body.title: Show me the math: Rohan's HRA in Pune

children.text: Rohan pays ₹22,000 a month for a flat in Baner. From tax year 2026-27, Pune is one of the eight cities where the third limit is 50% of salary. For HRA purposes, his salary here is his basic pay of ₹6,00,000 a year.

content.caption: Use 40% instead of 50% outside the eight listed cities

children.text: Rent is the binding limit for Rohan. If he moved to a costlier flat, his exemption would rise until it hit the ₹3,00,000 ceiling set by limits 1 and 3.

stats.label: HRA received
stats.context: Full year, all counted as salary

children.text: What the Exemption Is Worth in Rupees

An exemption does not hand you cash. It lowers your taxable income, so the saving equals the exempt amount multiplied by your tax rate, plus 4% health and education cess. Under the old regime, income above ₹5 lakh is taxed at 20% and income above ₹10 lakh at 30%.

body.title: Tax saved on ₹2,04,000 of exempt HRA

children.text: At the 30% slab, ₹2,04,000 × 30% × 1.04 = ₹63,648 a year. At the 20% slab it is ₹42,432. If the exemption pulls part of your income from the 30% slab into the 20% slab, the real saving falls between the two figures.

body.text: HRA exemption is only available under the old tax regime. The new tax regime under Section 202 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 115BAC of the 1961 Act) is the default. If you never tell your employer you want the old regime, every rupee of your HRA is taxed, even if you pay rent. Whether the old regime is worth it for you is covered in our course on choosing between the two regimes.

body.title: Quick Check: HRA Without Rent
body.question: Sneha works in Hyderabad, is on the old tax regime and receives ₹20,000 a month as HRA. She lives in a flat she bought in Gachibowli and pays no rent. How much of her HRA is tax-free?
options: All of it, because HRA is a housing allowance
50% of it, because Hyderabad is on the 50% list
40% of it, because she owns her home
body.explanation: The exemption applies only when you actually pay rent for the home you live in. With zero rent, the second limit (rent minus 10% of salary) is zero, so the lowest of the three limits is zero. Her entire ₹2,40,000 of HRA is taxable. Her home loan may bring other tax benefits, which Lesson 10 covers.

children.text: The Rules Around HRA Have Shifted Recently
If you learned about HRA from a colleague or an old blog post, parts of what you know may be out of date. The timeline below shows the changes that shape how HRA works for you today.

events.title: New tax regime introduced
events.description: An optional regime with lower slab rates arrived, but without most exemptions, including HRA.

events.title: New regime becomes the default
events.description: Salaried employees who did not choose the old regime were placed in the new regime, losing HRA exemption by default.

events.title: Central government HRA rises to 30%, 20% and 10%
events.description: Dearness allowance crossed 50%, triggering the higher HRA rates under the 7th Pay Commission.

events.title: Labour Codes come into force
events.description: Basic pay, dearness allowance and retaining allowance must make up at least 50% of total remuneration, pushing many employers to restructure salaries.

events.title: Income-tax Act, 2025 takes effect
events.description: HRA exemption moves to Schedule III (Table: S. No. 11). Form 124 replaces Form 12BB for declaring rent to your employer.

events.title: Eight cities qualify for the 50% limit
events.description: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad join Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai. Other cities stay at 40%.

children.text: Why a Salary Restructure Can Change Your HRA

markDefs.definition: Under the Labour Codes, basic pay plus dearness allowance plus retaining allowance. Allowances beyond 50% of total remuneration are added back to wages when calculating PF, gratuity and similar benefits.

children.text: Under the Labour Codes, allowances such as HRA and special allowance cannot exceed 50% of total remuneration. Any excess is treated as
wages

for PF and gratuity purposes. Many companies responded by raising basic salary. Because HRA is usually a percentage of basic, and two of the three exemption limits are also based on salary, a restructure can move your taxable HRA even when your CTC stays the same.

body.title: Scenario: Same Rent, New Salary Structure
body.scenario: Arjun works for an IT services firm in Chennai, is on the old regime and pays ₹25,000 a month in rent. Before the restructure, his basic was ₹35,000 a month with HRA at 50% of basic (₹17,500). After the restructure, his basic is ₹50,000 a month and HRA is still 50% of basic (₹25,000). His special allowance was cut so that his CTC is unchanged.
body.prompt: Work out Arjun's annual exempt HRA and taxable HRA before and after the restructure. Did the change help or hurt him on HRA?
body.modelAnswer: Before: HRA received ₹2,10,000; rent minus 10% of salary is ₹3,00,000 minus ₹42,000 = ₹2,58,000; 50% of salary is ₹2,10,000. The lowest is ₹2,10,000, so all of his HRA was tax-free and taxable HRA was nil. After: HRA received ₹3,00,000; rent minus 10% of salary is ₹3,00,000 minus ₹60,000 = ₹2,40,000; 50% of salary is ₹3,00,000. The lowest is ₹2,40,000, so exempt HRA rises by ₹30,000, but ₹60,000 of HRA is now taxable. On HRA he is better off: his tax-free amount went up by ₹30,000. The extra pay moved into basic and HRA came out of special allowance, which was fully taxable anyway, so ignoring PF, his taxable salary falls by ₹30,000. Notice that the limit holding him back has changed from 50% of salary to rent, so from now on only a higher rent, not a higher HRA, would raise his exemption. The higher basic also raises his PF contribution, which reduces his monthly take-home pay.

body.title: Try It: Meera in Ahmedabad
body.prompt: Meera works in Ahmedabad in tax year 2026-27 and is on the old regime. Her basic salary is ₹40,000 a month, her HRA is ₹18,000 a month and she pays ₹20,000 a month in rent. What is her annual exempt HRA in rupees?
body.explanation: Limit 1: HRA received is ₹2,16,000. Limit 2: rent of ₹2,40,000 minus 10% of salary (₹48,000) is ₹1,92,000. Limit 3: Ahmedabad is on the 50% list from tax year 2026-27, so 50% of ₹4,80,000 is ₹2,40,000. The lowest is ₹1,92,000. The remaining ₹24,000 of her HRA is taxable. In tax year 2025-26, Ahmedabad was still a 40% city, which would have made limit 3 ₹1,92,000, giving the same answer in her case.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: Where HRA Lives in the New Law
body.textWithBlank: Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, the HRA exemption is found in Schedule ___ (Table: S. No. 11), replacing Section 10(13A) of the old Act.
body.explanation: Schedule III of the Income-tax Act, 2025 lists exemptions for salaried employees. HRA sits at serial number 11. Payslips, employer tax sheets and older articles will still say 10(13A) for some time, so it helps to recognise both.

children.text: Find HRA in Your Own Salary

body.title: Five-Minute HRA Check on Your Payslip
steps: Download your latest payslip and note the monthly Basic salary and House Rent Allowance figures
Divide HRA by Basic to see whether your employer pays 40%, 50% or some other percentage
Check which tax regime you declared to your employer this year on the HR portal. If you did nothing, you are in the new regime
Open the monthly tax computation sheet on the HR portal and look for an HRA exemption line. If it shows zero while you pay rent, find out why
Write down your monthly rent and your city, and whether your city is one of the eight on the 50% list. You will need these numbers in Chapter 2

body.label: Income Tax Department e-filing portal
body.description: The official portal for filing returns, viewing your Annual Information Statement and using the department's tax calculators to compare the old and new regimes.

cards.definition: A salary component paid by an employer towards the cost of renting a home. It is fully taxable unless the HRA exemption applies.
The part of HRA treated as tax-free: the lowest of actual HRA, rent minus 10% of salary, and 50% or 40% of salary. Available only under the old regime to employees who pay rent.
The provision of the Income-tax Act, 2025 that grants the HRA exemption. It replaces Section 10(13A) of the Income-tax Act, 1961.
The default regime under Section 202 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 115BAC of the 1961 Act), with lower rates but no HRA exemption.
From tax year 2026-27: Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad. All other cities use 40%.
Basic pay plus dearness allowance plus retaining allowance, which must be at least 50% of total remuneration since 21 November 2025.

points: HRA is a salary allowance paid for housing. You receive it whether or not you pay rent, and it is taxable unless the exemption applies
The tax-free part is the lowest of actual HRA, rent minus 10% of salary, and 50% or 40% of salary, under Schedule III (Table: S. No. 11) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, formerly Section 10(13A)
The exemption works only under the old tax regime. The new regime is the default, so employees who pay rent must actively choose the old regime to use it
The value of the exemption is the exempt amount multiplied by your slab rate plus 4% cess, which can be over ₹60,000 a year for someone in the 30% slab
From tax year 2026-27, eight cities qualify for the 50% limit, including Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad
Salary restructuring under the Labour Codes can change your HRA and your exemption even when your CTC stays the same
